summary: Two new entities are proposed, both conf low. A pale far willow (S1.tree.far_willow_34995): t6 folded its fan into the near willow's note, but the fan converges on its own point. The open floor behind the yard where the roller stands (S1.grd.floor_behind_yard_34285): t5 left it to structures_e, who did not record it. One duplicate in disguise: S1.str.posts_35075's east post and S1.fig.figure_in_shed_35108 are the same indigo-tinted inverted-V strokes; the figure reading is the stronger one. A painted post named only in a group note becomes the SE corner post of S1.bld.farmhouse_thatched_33955. The 'small shed' at the yard's west side is that house's east hip end, not a separate building. One point on the wrong stroke: S1.bld.farmhouse_thatched_34600's ridge_w sat on an elm stem, 45 px west of the roof. Two notes were mangled by the merge's renameRefs. The flagged doubts answered: the hump is not a stack; the yard's hedge is bushes; the dome has no post (a stack); the roller and the crossing stems agree. The bending farmer, the yard objects, the pale bird, the lean-to and the long roof's material stay open, with evidence added. For the lead: S1.road.main runs through nine trunk feet in front of the farmsteads.

entities.name: pale far willow crown behind the long farmhouse
entities.what: A small fan of long thin shoots drawn in pale grey ink, rising up and out to the north-west from a point just above the long farmhouse's ridge and the far roof's east slope: a far pollarded willow (willow_fan form, drawn small and pale for distance) standing behind the farmstead, its head and trunk hidden by the roofs. Early spring, bare or a faint haze.

changes.add_note: SECOND PASS (farms), the hump: it is not a free-standing stack. At zoom 1.7-2.6 (hump_hp.jpg, hump_z.jpg, h1_norm.jpg) its outline is one crisp, smooth line from (33430, 845) up through (33500, 800) to (33560, 778), where it meets S1.bld.farmhouse_gable_33670's west eave corner (33575, 772). The surface inside is the same short slanted dashes as the rest of the band and as the thatch on the gable house's east slope (33680-33760, v 780-850), with no boundary between them. The band's lower edge is a straight dark line at v 867-881 (33430-33780), with a paler strip below it (v 881-899) and then the ground line. Nothing separates the hump from the band, so no prop is proposed. The evidence leans two ways. In the WEST (33400-33780) it favours reading (b): the smooth outline and the thatch dashes make the hump the west hip of a low thatched roof, with its eave at v ~875 (the front slope of the gable house's roof, or a low thatched wing in front of S1.bld.farmhouse_back_33450). In the EAST (33780-34150) it favours reading (a): S1.bld.farmhouse_thatched_33955's east hip ends at a corner post at (34142, 848-887) (see that entity), while the band runs on below the corner to v ~890, so there it stands in front of the wall line. The builder must not settle this silently. If the lead takes (b) for the west part, this line would start at u ~33780, and the west part becomes roof (a building entity, or eaves of S1.bld.farmhouse_gable_33670 lowered to v ~875).

for_lead.detail: Nine tree bases in front of the farmsteads lie between S1.road.main's edge_n and edge_s, five of them on or south of its centre line: elm_forked_33433 (905; n 893 / c 925 / s 960), elm_forked_33785 (935; 900/924/951), elm_tall_33865 (940; 902/925/952), elm_slender_33906 (935; 902/926/953), elm_twin_33936 (925; 902/926/954), elm_spreading_34030 (912 est; 903/928/958), bare_elm_twin_34552 (936; 916/938/960), bare_elm_twin_34640 (936; 916/937/960), bare_elm_tall_34703 (925 est; 917/936/960). On the scan (gl_ov.jpg, gl2_ov.jpg, zoom 2.6) the trunks stand on the light strip between the fences' feet (v ~895-918) and the top of the yard bank's dark face (v ~943-950). Either the route's walkable line weaves between them (a build choice), or its centre moves to the bank's top just south of the trunk feet (v ~945-950) with edge_n on the trunk feet. lessons: Compare low-confidence figures against posts and poles, not only against things of their own kind. On S1's threshing floor a figure (t6) and a structure's post (structures_e) were the same inverted-V strokes. The tool's near-duplicate check compares one kind, and the merge's cross-kind search paired rock/prop, roof/stack and hedge/tree, but not person/post. For every figure with conf low, list the posts, poles and frame points of structures within 20 px of its head-foot span.

On worn silk, colour separates a garment from a post. In S1 the painter tints clothing with indigo, while posts, poles and twigs are plain grey-black ink. Read a doubtful upright in natural colour at zoom 3-4 (scroll_inspect at half 45-60) before calling it a post or a figure. Also check whether a shaft continues to the ground: a post's does.

A pale crown with its own convergence point is its own tree. Far willows are drawn in pale grey wash beside a near willow's dark fan, and a tile agent may fold them into the near tree's note as 'fainter shoots'. Trace each fan to where its shoots converge, on a greyscale crop at zoom 3. Two convergence points 100+ px apart are two trees.

After the merge, test the route against the ground points. List every tree base and prop base that lies between the route's edge_n and edge_s. In S1 nine trunk feet stand in the road strip in front of the farmsteads, because the only level ground there is the trees' strip. The route's walkable line is then a choice for the lead, not a stroke reading.

In merge_fixes.mjs, rename references before writing MERGE notes that name the retired IDs (or skip notes in the rename). S1's renameRefs rewrote two retirement notes so that they named their own entity as retired.
